scenario.name: Microsoft WER, Mandiant & Elastic DFIR — IFEO SilentProcessExit & WerFault.exe LSASS Dump Hijack (Sysmon EID 12 / 13)
scenario.overview: Imagine an intruder who wants a complete photograph of the central credential guardroom without ever opening a suspicious camera lens directly at the guardroom door. Instead, the intruder flips two official diagnostic switches on the building own built-in crash-inspector board so the operating system Error Reporting clerk itself politely photographs the entire guardroom memory into a chosen folder whenever a silent-exit bell is rung. In this scenario (T1546.012, Microsoft WER, Mandiant & Elastic DFIR, IFEO SilentProcessExit & WerFault.exe LSASS Dump Hijack (Sysmon EID 12 / 13)), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: enabling IFEO (FLG_MONITOR_SILENT_PROCESS_EXIT), then configuring SilentProcessExit\lsass.exe (LAUNCH_NOTIFYPROCESS | LOCAL_DUMP), then triggering RtlReportSilentProcessExit (Source: Winlogon / SilentProcessExit). Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Enabling IFEO (FLG_MONITOR_SILENT_PROCESS_EXIT), then Configuring SilentProcessExit\lsass.exe (LAUNCH_NOTIFYPROCESS | LOCAL_DUMP), then Triggering RtlReportSilentProcessExit (Source: Winlogon / SilentProcessExit). Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 13 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Enabling IFEO FLG_MONITOR_SILENT_PROCESS_EXIT (0x200) on lsass.exe (Sysmon EventID 13)
stages.subtitle: Persistence (T1546.012 - Event Triggered Execution: Image File Execution Options Injection)
stages.description: Walking up to the system debugging switchboard, the intruder flips on the special silent-exit watch flag specifically targeting the credential guardroom so the operating system watches for exit notifications on that process. To avoid opening a direct suspicious handle to lsass.exe from an untrusted binary, the attacker configures HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution Options\lsass.exe\GlobalFlag = 0x00000200 (FLG_MONITOR_SILENT_PROCESS_EXIT). Sysmon EventID 13 logs the exact DWORD modification (logged in Sysmon Event 13 with EventID=13 , Sysmon Registry Value Set, TargetObject=HKLM\...\Image File Execution Options\lsass.exe\GlobalFlag, FlagValue=0x00000200 , FLG_MONITOR_SILENT_PROCESS_EXIT so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes reg.exe add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution Options\lsass.exe" /v GlobalFlag /t REG_DWORD /d 512 /f (which Modifies or queries Windows Registry keys and values , reg.exe add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution Options\ so that manipulates persistent Windows Registry configuration or credential material , T1546.012 during "Enabling IFEO FLG_MONITOR_SILENT_PROCESS_EXIT , 0x200 on lsass.exe , Sysmon EventID 13" to establish persistence, alter system behavior, or harvest secrets). Next, the follow-up artifact Flag Constant: FLG_MONITOR_SILENT_PROCESS_EXIT = 0x200 (512 decimal) runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Flag Constant: FLG_MONITOR_SILENT_PROCESS_EXIT = 0x200 , 512 decimal via System / Runtime Ex so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1546.012 during "Enabling IFEO FLG_MONITOR_SILENT_PROCESS_EXIT , 0x200 on lsass.exe , Sysmon EventID 13" , To avoid opening a direct suspicious handle to lsass while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ reg.exe add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution Options\lsass.exe" /v GlobalFlag /t REG_DWORD /d 512 /f / ⇠#1 ACK 13) from Node ① (#1 Attacker Registry Modification) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 WerFault.exe (Trusted Dumper)).

stages.subtitle: Credential Access (T1003.001 - SilentProcessExit LocalDumpFolder & MonitorProcess)

Next, the attacker creates HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\SilentProcessExit\lsass.exe and sets ReportingMode=2 (LAUNCH_NOTIFYPROCESS | LOCAL_DUMP), LocalDumpFolder="C:\Windows\Temp\Dumps", DumpType=2 (Full Memory Minidump), and MonitorProcess="C:\ProgramData\beacon.exe" (logged in Sysmon Event 13 with EventID=13 , Sysmon Registry Value Set, RegistryKey=HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\SilentProcessExit\lsass.exe, LocalDumpFolder=C:\Windows\Temp\Dumps, DumpType=0x2 , MiniDumpWithFullMemory so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ reg.exe add "...\SilentProcessExit\lsass.exe" /v LocalDumpFolder /d C:\Windows\Temp\Dumps / ⇠#2 ACK 13) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 IFEO GlobalFlag (0x200)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 WerFault.exe (Trusted Dumper)).

stages.title: Stage 3: Triggering RtlReportSilentProcessExit & WerFault.exe Full LSASS Dump (Application EventID 3001)
stages.subtitle: Credential Access (T1003.001 - Trusted WerFault.exe Proxy Dumping LSASS)
stages.description: Finally, the intruder taps the undocumented silent-exit chime inside a tiny helper tool. Hearing the chime, the signed Microsoft Error Reporting clerk itself marches over, dumps the entire live LSASS credential memory cleanly into the attacker folder, and leaves LSASS running completely undisturbed. The attacker calls ntdll.dll!RtlReportSilentProcessExit(hLsass, 0) (which only requires PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION | PROCESS_VM_READ or is triggered via CreateRemoteThread/NtTerminateProcess on a helper). The Windows Error Reporting service spawns the Microsoft-signed C:\Windows\System32\WerFault.exe, which dumps lsass.exe-(PID).dmp into C:\Windows\Temp\Dumps, spawns MonitorProcess, and logs Application EventID 3001 (Source: Winlogon / SilentProcessExit) (logged in Sysmon Event 10 with EventID=10 , ProcessAccess + 11 , FileCreate + 3001 , Application Log, ProxyBinary=C:\Windows\System32\WerFault.exe , Microsoft Signed, TargetProcess=C:\Windows\System32\lsass.exe, CreatedDumpFile=C:\Windows\Temp\Dumps\lsass.exe-684.dmp so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes ntdll!RtlReportSilentProcessExit(hProcess, 0) -> LPC message to WerSvcGroup (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ntdll!RtlReportSilentProcessExit, hProcess, 0 -> LPC message to WerSvcGroup via System / Run so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1003.001 during "Triggering RtlReportSilentProcessExit & WerFault.exe Full LSASS Dump , Application EventID 3001" , The attacker calls ntdll while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact Sysmon EventID 10: SourceImage=C:\Windows\System32\WerFault.exe TargetImage=C:\Windows\System32\lsass.exe GrantedAccess=0x1FFFFF runs (which invokes or targets the host daemon/process , Sysmon EventID 10: SourceImage=C:\Windows\System32\WerFault.exe TargetImage=C:\Windows\System32\lsass. so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1003.001 during "Triggering RtlReportSilentProcessExit & WerFault.exe Full LSASS Dump , Application EventID 3001" , The attacker calls ntdll while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ C:\Windows\System32\WerFault.exe -u -p 684 -s 1420 (Dumping lsass.exe via SilentProcessExit) / ⇠#3 ACK 10) from Node ③ (#3 IFEO GlobalFlag (0x200)) to Node ④ (#4 SilentProcessExit\lsass.exe), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 WerFault.exe (Trusted Dumper)).

steps.simpleExplanation: Next, the attacker creates HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\SilentProcessExit\lsass.exe and sets ReportingMode=2 (LAUNCH_NOTIFYPROCESS | LOCAL_DUMP), LocalDumpFolder="C:\Windows\Temp\Dumps", DumpType=2 (Full Memory Minidump), and MonitorProcess="C:\ProgramData\beacon.exe" (logged in Sysmon Event 13 with EventID=13 , Sysmon Registry Value Set, RegistryKey=HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\SilentProcessExit\lsass.exe, LocalDumpFolder=C:\Windows\Temp\Dumps, DumpType=0x2 , MiniDumpWithFullMemory so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Under the hood, the observed step executes reg.exe add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\SilentProcessExit\lsass.exe" /v ReportingMode /t REG_DWORD /d 2 /f (which Modifies or queries Windows Registry keys and values , reg.exe add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\SilentProcessExit\lsass.exe" so that manipulates persistent Windows Registry configuration or credential material , T1003.001 during "Configuring SilentProcessExit\lsass.exe LocalDumpFolder, DumpType=2 & MonitorProcess , Sysmon EventID 13" to establish persistence, alter system behavior, or harvest secrets). Next, the follow-up artifact reg.exe add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\SilentProcessExit\lsass.exe" /v LocalDumpFolder /t REG_SZ /d "C:\Windows\Temp\Dumps" /f runs (which Modifies or queries Windows Registry keys and values , reg.exe add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\SilentProcessExit\lsass.exe" so that manipulates persistent Windows Registry configuration or credential material , T1003.001 during "Configuring SilentProcessExit\lsass.exe LocalDumpFolder, DumpType=2 & MonitorProcess , Sysmon EventID 13" to establish persistence, alter system behavior, or harvest secrets).
steps.diagramAlignment: On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 across the topology from Attacker Registry Modification and IFEO GlobalFlag , 0x200 toward SilentProcessExit\lsass.exe and Sysmon EID 12/13 & Application.
steps.detectionAndEvidence: Documented in Sysmon Event 13 (recording EventID=13 , Sysmon Registry Value Set, RegistryKey=HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\SilentProcessExit\lsass.exe, LocalDumpFolder=C:\Windows\Temp\Dumps, DumpType=0x2 , MiniDumpWithFullMemory under T1003.001): Alert on any registry write under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\SilentProcessExit\* or HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\Windows Error Reporting\LocalDumps\*.

steps.plainTitle: Triggering RtlReportSilentProcessExit & WerFault.exe Full LSASS Dump (Application EventID 3001)
steps.storyAnalogy: Finally, the intruder taps the undocumented silent-exit chime inside a tiny helper tool. Hearing the chime, the signed Microsoft Error Reporting clerk itself marches over, dumps the entire live LSASS credential memory cleanly into the attacker folder, and leaves LSASS running completely undisturbed.
steps.simpleExplanation: The attacker calls ntdll.dll!RtlReportSilentProcessExit(hLsass, 0) (which only requires PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION | PROCESS_VM_READ or is triggered via CreateRemoteThread/NtTerminateProcess on a helper). The Windows Error Reporting service spawns the Microsoft-signed C:\Windows\System32\WerFault.exe, which dumps lsass.exe-(PID).dmp into C:\Windows\Temp\Dumps, spawns MonitorProcess, and logs Application EventID 3001 (Source: Winlogon / SilentProcessExit) (logged in Sysmon Event 10 with EventID=10 , ProcessAccess + 11 , FileCreate + 3001 , Application Log, ProxyBinary=C:\Windows\System32\WerFault.exe , Microsoft Signed, TargetProcess=C:\Windows\System32\lsass.exe, CreatedDumpFile=C:\Windows\Temp\Dumps\lsass.exe-684.dmp so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Under the hood, the observed step executes ntdll!RtlReportSilentProcessExit(hProcess, 0) -> LPC message to WerSvcGroup (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ntdll!RtlReportSilentProcessExit, hProcess, 0 -> LPC message to WerSvcGroup via System / Run so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1003.001 during "Triggering RtlReportSilentProcessExit & WerFault.exe Full LSASS Dump , Application EventID 3001" , The attacker calls ntdll while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact Sysmon EventID 10: SourceImage=C:\Windows\System32\WerFault.exe TargetImage=C:\Windows\System32\lsass.exe GrantedAccess=0x1FFFFF runs (which invokes or targets the host daemon/process , Sysmon EventID 10: SourceImage=C:\Windows\System32\WerFault.exe TargetImage=C:\Windows\System32\lsass. so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1003.001 during "Triggering RtlReportSilentProcessExit & WerFault.exe Full LSASS Dump , Application EventID 3001" , The attacker calls ntdll while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution).
steps.diagramAlignment: On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 across the topology from Attacker Registry Modification and IFEO GlobalFlag , 0x200 toward SilentProcessExit\lsass.exe and Sysmon EID 12/13 & Application.
steps.detectionAndEvidence: Documented in Sysmon Event 10 (recording EventID=10 , ProcessAccess + 11 , FileCreate + 3001 , Application Log, ProxyBinary=C:\Windows\System32\WerFault.exe , Microsoft Signed, TargetProcess=C:\Windows\System32\lsass.exe, CreatedDumpFile=C:\Windows\Temp\Dumps\lsass.exe-684.dmp under T1003.001): Do not blindly exclude WerFault.exe or wermgr.exe from Sysmon EventID 10 (TargetImage=lsass.exe) or EventID 11 (*.dmp creation); correlate WerFault.exe LSASS access against SilentProcessExit registry keys.
